documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Press Release / Media Release
Audited Financial Results For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) achieved a record annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT in FY26, operating at 112% of installed capacity. The company reported a full-year GRM of $9.20 per barrel and a Q4 GRM of $13.75 per barrel, outperforming Singapore benchmarks. CPCL is undertaking capex projects including a Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project worth INR 1,600 crores and a retail outlet rollout worth INR 400 crores. The Board recommended a total dividend of INR 62 per share for FY26. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its Q4 FY25 and full year financial and operational performance, highlighting a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT and a full-year GRM of $4.22 per barrel.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects its operational and financial performance momentum to continue into the new financial year.
guidance.quote: To summarize, we continue to deliver resilient operational and financial performance and see the momentum to continue in the new financial year as well.

demand_outlook.claim: The southern Indian market shows a clear shortfall in Motor Spirit (MS), where production is less than demand by close to 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor Spirit demand growth in the southern market is projected around 4% to 5%, while HSD growth is forecasted at 3%.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred a capital expenditure of INR 856 crores in FY26 compared to INR 673 crores in FY25.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project execution requires a capex of INR 1,600 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL's retail outlet project involves an outlay of INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: The new LOBS unit will add 250 KTPA of fresh Group 2 and Group 3 capacity.
capex_expansion.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capex_expansion.claim: Hexane production capacity has been expanded from 30 to 60.
capex_expansion.quote: It was 30, now the capacity is 60.

capex_expansion.claim: The company spent Rs. 673 crores as capital expenditure for the current financial year.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: Maintenance capex is expected to remain in the Rs. 200-250 crore range.
capex_expansion.quote: Our maintenance CAPEX remains Rs. 200-250 crore range, and the next year forecast also, we feel the CAPEX will be in that range.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the CBR project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CBR update, in the last year we revised the capital cost as well as the capital structure. The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: The new refinery project has a capacity of 9 million metric tons and a polypropylene petrochemical intensity of 6%.
capex_expansion.quote: The new refinery capital cost is Rs 36,000 Crore approximately, 9 million metric ton capacity and petrochemical intensity of 6% and which is PP, polypropylene.

margins_costs.claim: In Q4 FY26, CPCL's GRM stood at $13.75 per barrel against the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: Core GRM for Q4 FY26 was $10.30 per barrel.
CPCL recorded a forex loss of approximately INR 200 crores for Q4 FY26 and around INR 350 crores for the full year.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: Niche products constitute 7% to 8% of volume and contribute around 15% of CPCL's margins.
margins_costs.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7%–8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins.

margins_costs.claim: The full-year GRM for 2024-25 stood at $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: The inventory gain for the fourth quarter was $0.66 per barrel, amounting to Rs. 125 crores.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: The annual inventory resulted in a loss of $0.06 per barrel, totaling Rs. 40 crores.
margins_costs.quote: But on an overall annual basis, the inventory would be a loss that is $ 0.06 per barrel, Rs. 40 crores in amount.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a total gross refining margin of 3.40 $/BBl for 9M 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL processed a record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT in FY26, equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL processed 2.93 MMT of crude throughput in Q4 FY26, operating at 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: Annual production reached record levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel and 1.318 MMT for petrol in FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a record LPG production of 447 TMT in FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: Distillate yield reached a record high of 79.1% during FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for the year, equivalent to 99.5% of its installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year

orders_capacity.claim: Crude throughput for Quarter 4 was 2.974 MMT, representing 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL's crude basket size covers 156 numbers of crudes from all regions.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL Crude basket size : 156 nos covering crudes from all regions.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL reduced its gross debt-to-equity ratio to 0.18 from 0.39 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings stood at INR 1,900 crores, while net borrowings were INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL paid a total dividend of INR 62 per share for FY26, comprising an interim dividend of INR 8 and a recommended final dividend of INR 54.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: The board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value for the current year.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: As of March 31, 2025, total debt stood at an absolute level of Rs. 3,100 crores with a net worth of Rs. 7,939 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024. Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

risks_headwinds.claim: Logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility present operational challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL experienced a short-term supply disturbance of 30% to 40% from Middle East term contracts.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to the volatility of crude prices pose a challenge to operations.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects to see significant commissioning from its 300 retail outlet licenses in FY27.
management_commitments.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: The company aims to bring fuel and loss down to very efficient levels on a sustained basis.
management_commitments.quote: we went to a roadmap where we said on a sustained basis, we will bring it down to very efficient levels

management_commitments.claim: Management remains focused on operational efficiency, safety, and capital discipline to honor commitments of long-term value creation.
management_commitments.quote: we remain focused on things we control that is fuel efficiency, capacity utilisation and operating our refinery efficiently in a safe, reliable, and environmentally responsible manner and continue to focus on key metrics of controlling the operating cost as well as maintaining capital discipline by adhering to optimum return on value added and growth projects and thereby honouring our commitment to create long-term value for shareholders.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
